bib.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

question: How well do language models use information placed at different positions in long input contexts?
hypothesis: If models robustly use long contexts, performance should be minimally affected by the position of the relevant information.
contributions: Controlled multi-document QA and synthetic key-value retrieval experiments varying context length and position of relevant information, showing a U-shaped curve
Preliminary study of architecture, query-aware contextualization and instruction fine-tuning
Open-domain QA case study showing reader accuracy saturates before retriever recall
New evaluation protocol: minimal gap between best- and worst-case position

method.summary: Six LLMs are prompted (no training) with k NaturalQuestions-Open passages, exactly one containing the answer, whose position is varied; a synthetic UUID key-value retrieval task is used likewise. Accuracy is whether a gold answer appears in the output.
method.task: multi-document QA, key-value retrieval, open-domain QA (retriever-reader)

datasets.name: NaturalQuestions-Open (multi-document QA)
datasets.split: queries whose annotated long answer is a paragraph
datasets.source: Lee et al. 2019; Kwiatkowski et al. 2019; Wikipedia dump from late 2018, passages of at most 100 tokens
datasets.preprocessing: Answer doc = NQ annotated paragraph; k-1 distractors = top Contriever (MS-MARCO fine-tuned) chunks not containing any annotated answer, ordered by decreasing relevance

datasets.name: Synthetic key-value retrieval
datasets.size: 500 examples per setting; 75, 140 and 300 key-value pairs
datasets.source: JSON of random 128-bit UUID keys and values
datasets.preprocessing: position of the queried key varied

models.name: MPT-30B-Instruct
models.init_from: MPT-30B, pre-trained on 1T tokens at 2048 then 50B tokens at 8192

inference.samples: one greedy output per item; no seeds or repeats stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot instruction prompt, same standard prompt for each model (Fig 2); query after the documents; query-aware variant puts query before and after
inference.retrieval: Contriever top-k for open-domain QA, k from 5 to 50; 10, 20, 30 documents in controlled task

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: any correct annotated answer appears in the predicted output

metrics.name: retriever recall
metrics.definition: fraction of questions where retrieved docs contain an answer (as plotted)

eval.protocol: accuracy per answer position; no significance tests or repeats stated

limits: Only NaturalQuestions-Open and a synthetic UUID task; exactly one relevant document, unlike real retrieval
Greedy decoding only; other decoding left to future work
Architecture, query-aware and instruction-tuning analyses are described as preliminary
GPT-4 evaluated only on a 500-example subset at 20 documents because the full run would cost upwards of $6000
Closed API models (0613 versions, Claude-1.3) are no longer current; no repeats or significance tests
Prompt-based, no training; mechanisms are hypothesized, not tested
